_why: A message template is rendered into the terminal, into --json, and into the --report
Markdown a developer pastes into a support thread. Any placeholder that can carry a
credential is therefore a leak in three places at once.
A full URL is the dangerous one and the easy one to miss: an out-of-scope entry such as
https://secret@internal-gateway.example/mcp carries its credential in the userinfo. The
host rule stops us SENDING a key there; only this stops us PRINTING one.
So templates interpolate {host}, never {url}. Enforced by validate_contract.py, which
rejects any template using a forbidden name — the rule cannot be reintroduced by a
well-meaning edit to a single message.

_readme: Every finding either implementation can emit is defined here and nowhere else.
Ids are stable and greppable: changing one is a breaking change to the --json contract.
`message` and `remediation` are templates; {placeholders} are filled from the finding's
`data` object. Both languages must render the same string from the same data, which the
`auto_fixable` is a property of the DEFECT; whether a fix actually runs also requires the
client registry to permit that fix_kind for that client (see clients/*.json → repairs).

defects.title: Connected to SuperDocs
defects.message: {client}: connected to SuperDocs ({tools} tools, {prompts} prompts)

defects.title: Configuration file cannot be read
defects.message: {client}: cannot read {path} ({reason})
defects.remediation: Check the file's permissions, then run mcp-doctor again.

defects.title: Configuration file is not valid
defects.message: {client}: {path} is not valid {format} (line {line}, column {column}: {reason})
defects.remediation: Repair the syntax by hand. mcp-doctor never rewrites a file it cannot parse.

defects.title: Configuration file is empty
defects.message: {client}: {path} exists but is empty
defects.remediation: Nothing is configured yet. Add a SuperDocs server entry for this client.
defects.note: Distinct from invalid-syntax on purpose. Both of Antigravity's mcp_config.json files on the machine this was written against were 0 bytes — a freshly installed client, not a corrupted one. Reporting 'invalid JSON at line 1 column 1' would be technically true and useless.

defects.title: No SuperDocs entry configured
defects.message: {client}: no SuperDocs server configured in {path}
defects.remediation: Add a SuperDocs server entry for this client. A key must be resolvable from {key_env}.

defects.title: More than one SuperDocs entry
defects.message: {client}: {count} SuperDocs entries found in {path} ({names})
defects.remediation: Remove the entries you do not want. mcp-doctor will not guess which to keep.

defects.title: Repeated key in the configuration
defects.message: {client}: '{field_name}' appears more than once in {container}; the last one wins and the earlier value is ignored
defects.remediation: Remove the duplicate. A stale value sitting above a good one is invisible to the client and to this tool.
defects.note: JSON has no duplicate-key error: parsers silently keep the last. A wrong url above a right one therefore looks like a working config that does not work. TOML rejects duplicates outright, so this only arises for JSON and JSONC. The placeholder is `field_name`, not `key`: the credential denylist bans `key` outright so that nobody has to judge, per message, whether a given {key} means a JSON field or an API key.

defects.title: Entry has a URL but is not an HTTP server
defects.message: {client}: the SuperDocs entry has a url but its transport is {found}, not {expected}
defects.remediation: Set the transport to {expected}.

defects.title: SuperDocs URL uses http://
defects.message: {client}: SuperDocs URL uses http:// — the endpoint requires https://
defects.remediation: Change the scheme to https://.

defects.title: Wrong path on the SuperDocs host
defects.message: {client}: SuperDocs URL path is {found}, expected {expected}
defects.remediation: Change the path to {expected}.

defects.title: Credentials embedded in the URL
defects.message: {client}: the SuperDocs URL contains embedded credentials
defects.remediation: Remove the credentials from the URL and supply the key as an Authorization header.

defects.title: SuperDocs entry has no URL
defects.message: {client}: the SuperDocs entry has no URL
defects.remediation: Set the URL to https://api.superdocs.app/mcp.

defects.title: SuperDocs URL has a query or fragment
defects.message: {client}: the SuperDocs URL must not contain a query string or fragment
defects.remediation: Use the bare endpoint https://api.superdocs.app/mcp.

defects.title: No Authorization header
defects.message: {client}: the SuperDocs entry has no Authorization header
defects.remediation: Add: Authorization: Bearer <your key>.

defects.title: Authorization header is missing the Bearer scheme
defects.message: {client}: the Authorization header does not start with 'Bearer '
defects.remediation: The value must be: Bearer <your key>.

defects.title: Authorization header says Bearer twice
defects.message: {client}: the Authorization header repeats the Bearer scheme
defects.remediation: The value must be: Bearer <your key>, once.

defects.title: Accept header cannot accept JSON
defects.message: {client}: the configured Accept header is {found}; SuperDocs requires it to include application/json
defects.remediation: Set Accept to application/json, or remove the override so the client sends its own.

defects.title: Environment variable is not set
defects.message: {client}: the entry references {variable}, which is not set in this environment
defects.remediation: Export {variable}, or replace the placeholder with a value the client can resolve.

defects.title: No key available
defects.message: {client}: no SuperDocs key found in the configuration or in {key_env}
defects.remediation: Create a key at https://docs.superdocs.app/account/api-keys and export it as {key_env}.

defects.title: Key does not look like a SuperDocs key
defects.message: {client}: the configured key does not begin with {expected_prefixes}
defects.remediation: SuperDocs keys begin with sk_ or lce_. Check you pasted the right value.

defects.title: Entry points somewhere other than SuperDocs
defects.message: {client}: SuperDocs entry points at host {host}, not the canonical endpoint. Left unchanged — mcp-doctor only diagnoses direct connections to {canonical_host}.
defects.note: THE HOST RULE. This entry is deliberate: a policy gateway, egress proxy, self-hosted relay, staging endpoint or mock server. Never repaired, never rewritten, never diagnosed.

defects.title: stdio server, out of scope
defects.message: {client}: the SuperDocs entry launches a local process; mcp-doctor v1 only diagnoses remote HTTP connections

defects.title: OAuth-configured entry, out of scope
defects.message: {client}: the SuperDocs entry uses an OAuth flow; mcp-doctor v1 only diagnoses static Bearer keys

defects.title: This client cannot send a SuperDocs key
defects.message: {client}: its remote-server configuration has no header mechanism, so a SuperDocs key cannot be supplied ({reason})
defects.remediation: Not fixable from here. Use a client that supports request headers, or put a gateway in front that adds the credential.
defects.note: Discovered while adding Antigravity: its shipped mcp_config.json documentation defines only `command`/`args`/`env` for stdio and `serverUrl` for SSE — no headers field anywhere. SuperDocs authenticates with `Authorization: Bearer`, so the honest answer is that the combination is not configurable, rather than emitting repair advice that cannot work.

defects.title: Unrecognised client
defects.message: {path}: parsed, but this client is not in the registry — reported only, never edited

defects.title: Host could not be resolved
defects.message: Cannot resolve {host} ({reason})
defects.remediation: Check your network connection and DNS settings.

defects.title: Connection failed
defects.message: Cannot connect to {host} ({reason})
defects.remediation: Check your network, VPN, or firewall. If you use an outbound proxy, confirm it permits {host}.

defects.title: TLS handshake failed
defects.message: TLS failure talking to {host} ({reason})
defects.remediation: A TLS-intercepting proxy or an out-of-date certificate store is the usual cause.

defects.title: Request timed out
defects.message: Timed out after {seconds}s talking to {host}
defects.remediation: Retry; if it persists, check for a slow or blocking network path.

defects.title: Something other than SuperDocs answered
defects.message: {host} returned {status} without the SuperDocs authentication header — a proxy or captive portal is answering instead of the endpoint
defects.remediation: This is a network interception, not a key problem. Do not rotate your key; check your proxy or network.
defects.note: Depends on the fingerprint in profile/superdocs.json → unauthenticated.fingerprint.

defects.title: Key rejected
defects.message: {client}: SuperDocs rejected the key (401)
defects.remediation: The key is missing, revoked or mistyped. Check or rotate it at https://docs.superdocs.app/account/api-keys.

defects.title: Key accepted but access denied
defects.message: {client}: SuperDocs accepted the key but denied access (403)
defects.remediation: The key is valid but lacks access. Check the account's plan and permissions.

defects.title: Negotiated a different protocol version
defects.message: Connected, but SuperDocs negotiated {found} where the profile recorded {expected}
defects.remediation: No action needed. The connection works; this is a dated observation, not a fault.

defects.title: Tool or prompt count changed
defects.message: Connected, but saw {tools} tools and {prompts} prompts where the profile recorded {expected_tools} and {expected_prompts}
defects.remediation: No action needed. Reported so a changed surface is visible, never as a failure.
